sources.cite: Amazon Route 53 Developer Guide, What is Amazon Route 53 Resolver?
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: 'Inbound Resolver endpoints allow DNS queries to your VPC from your on-premises network or another VPC'; 'Outbound Resolver endpoints allow DNS queries from your VPC to your on-premises network'; 'The on-premises DNS resolver has a forwarding rule that points queries to dev.example.com to an inbound endpoint'; VPC Resolver answers records in private hosted zones. That a private hosted zone answers only VPCs associated with it, and the endpoint's two-IP-addresses-in-two-Availability-Zones setup, are from memory of the Route 53 guide (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the solutions architect for Hollis Mills, a fictional manufacturer. The ERP database moved to Amazon RDS in the hub VPC; its name erp-db.corp.internal is a record in the private hosted zone corp.internal. At 18:00 the ERP application servers, still in the data center, switch their connection string to that name. A test from the data center just failed: the name does not resolve.
handover: The data center reaches the hub VPC over Direct Connect with a VPN backup; routing works (ping to the database's IP succeeds).
The hub VPC has an outbound Resolver endpoint, built last year so AWS workloads can resolve on-premises names.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the data center's DNS servers, the Resolver endpoints in the hub VPC and the private hosted zone.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

inbound.label: Create an inbound Resolver endpoint (two subnets, SG allowing DNS from 10.0.0.0/12), then a corp.internal conditional forwarder on both DC DNS servers

arch@cloudshell:~$ aws route53resolver create-resolver-endpoint --name hub-inbound --direction INBOUND --security-group-ids sg-dns-from-dc --ip-addresses SubnetId=subnet-hub-a,Ip=10.40.8.10 SubnetId=subnet-hub-b,Ip=10.40.9.10 ...

writeup.question: For the record: why the data center could not resolve the name, what you built, and why not a public record.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Distinguishes the record from the path to it.
parts.modelAnswer: The record exists and resolves inside the hub VPC. A private hosted zone answers only associated VPCs; the hub had only an outbound endpoint (AWS to data center) and the data center's DNS had no forwarder for corp.internal.

parts.label: What
parts.modelAnswer: An inbound Resolver endpoint with addresses in two Availability Zones and a security group allowing DNS from the data center, and a conditional forwarder for corp.internal on both DNS servers pointing at it.

parts.label: Not public
parts.modelAnswer: Publishing the record in the public zone would expose the database's name and address, and still not answer the configured name. Split-horizon keeps internal names in the private zone.

expertPath.text: Resolves in the VPC, NXDOMAIN from the data center; only an outbound endpoint; no corp.internal forwarder.
Inbound endpoint in two AZs; forwarders on both DNS servers; endpoint in code; probes from both sites and paths.

exposed.headline: Split-horizon, not one horizon
exposed.body: Private names belong in a private zone that only your networks can query. Give the data center a path to ask it (an inbound endpoint and a forwarder) instead of publishing internal records.

cutoverRolledBack.headline: The query had no way in
cutoverRolledBack.body: An outbound endpoint carries queries from AWS to the data center. For the data center to resolve a private hosted zone it needs an inbound endpoint and a conditional forwarder pointing at it.

resolving.headline: Good: the right direction
resolving.body: You saw the name worked inside the VPC and not outside, found only an outbound endpoint, added the inbound one with forwarders on both DNS servers, and tested both sites over both paths.

scoring.modelReasoning: The name resolves inside the hub VPC and not from the data center, so the record is fine and the path is missing: a private hosted zone answers only associated VPCs, and the only Resolver endpoint is outbound. Create an inbound endpoint in two Availability Zones and conditional forwarders for corp.internal on the data center's DNS servers. Publishing the record publicly exposes it and does not fix the configured name; associating another VPC does not help the data center.
